witness_description: No witness. The claim is a truncated sentence referring to a specific graph G and two 'exhibited' transitive reductions of G, none of which are supplied in the record, so there is no concrete object against which a counterexample could be checked.
refutation_explanation: The claim text ('We have exhibited two distinct transitive reductions of G, so the transitive reduction') is cut off before its conclusion and names external data (G and the two exhibited reductions) that the record does not contain. The logical schema 'two distinct transitive reductions exist => the transitive reduction is not unique' is a tautology; the only refutable content is whether the unsupplied exhibits are genuinely distinct transitive reductions of the actual G. A deterministic exact-arithmetic context sweep over all 69 labeled loop-free digraphs on n=1,2,3 vertices, enumerating all minimum-cardinality edge sets with the same reachability closure (Aho-Garey-Ullman transitive reduction), confirms by exhaustion that every acyclic digraph in that space has exactly one transitive reduction (so the premise is impossible if G is a DAG), while cyclic digraphs can have two or more (first in bitmask order: n=3, edges {(0,1),(0,2),(1,0)}, with two distinct minimum reductions {(0,1),(0,2),(1,0)} and {(0,1),(1,0),(1,2)}), so the premise is realizable for cyclic G. Without knowing G, no bounded search can refute the specific claim.
search_space: Context probe only (the specific claim supplies no finite instance): all 69 labeled directed graphs without self-loops on n = 1, 2, 3 vertices, and for each, exhaustive enumeration of all subsets of the n*(n-1) ordered pairs whose Warshall reachability closure matches, keeping the minimum-cardinality ones; fixed lexicographic bitmask iteration order, integer/frozenset arithmetic only.
